_comment: BAND-SPLIT-2. This band's own dialogue container. Same `{"conversations": {...}}` shape as opening.json/village.json/trainers.json/relay.json/stronghold.json/meadows_freed.json, merged onto the same table by scripts/story/dialogue_runner.gd::table() (EXTRA_DIALOGUE_PATHS). Unlike the four content configs BAND-SPLIT cut, this is a dictionary keyed by conversation id, not a positional array -- there is no `order` to preserve, because lookup is always by id and never by position. A trainer or NPC placed in band1_lower_meadows gets its dialogue written here instead of appended to trainers.json, so a band author never has to touch a file another band is also writing to.
_comment_tournament_1: TOURNAMENT-1 / FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. The village tournament's whole script, plus the South Bridge gatekeeper's. Halda is the marshal (data/config/village_npcs.json); her ordered `greeting_when` list uses existing progression flags, not a tournament state machine. Registration names the complete-team, camp, Creature Bed, rest/recovery and strength requirements and sets `opening:tournament_registered` -- and, per TOURNAMENT-FLOW-0903 below, so does every other branch that can be a player's first meeting with her, so a team that was ready before it ever met Halda is never sent through the registration speech at all. Each round is now TWO conversations, spoken by the OPPONENT rather than by Halda (the last voice the player hears should be the person about to send a creature out): the ring-entrance banter, which sets `tournament_<round>_at_ring` and starts nothing, and `tournament_<round>_begin`, the explicit 'begin the round' line that ends on `battle:<trainer_id>` -- owner playtest 2026-09-03 item 3's 'you enter then you choose to start the battle'.
_comment_tournament_flow_0903: TOURNAMENT-FLOW-0903, 2026-09-03. Two owner playtest findings, both about how the tournament FEELS to walk into rather than what it fights: (2) 'Starting the tournament was hard even after I had everything. I had to talk to the starter several times' -- village_npcs.json's Halda ladder put the registration briefing ahead of every readiness branch regardless of how ready the team already was, so a player who had already trained, fed, rested and camped a full team before ever meeting her still had to sit through the register speech and talk to her again before sign-up was even offered. Fixed by narrowing registration's own branch to the case it is actually for (`unless_flag` now also requires the team NOT be ready yet), so a team that is already ready meets whichever specific branch names it -- sign-up if everything holds, camp/condition/train otherwise -- in ONE visit. (3) 'you enter then you choose to start the battle then it announces you won and announces the next round' -- see the round comment above for the two-conversation split, and scripts/world/tournament.gd's `_announce_new_round_wins()`/`round_result_message()` for the win/next-round announcement, pushed through the same one-shot `Game.push_world_message()` toast every other world event already uses.
_comment_saddle: `tournament_halda_champion` is the NPC line the owner directive asks for: it says out loud that a Meadowhart can be ridden, and that the saddle needs rootstone from past the crossing. It does NOT carry a `flag:` effect -- the saddle pattern is granted by `tournament_final_oskar`'s own `reward.flags` the moment the final is won, so a player who never walks back to Halda still has it. The line explains the prize; it is not the prize. That split is deliberate: a reward that can only be collected by re-reading a conversation is a reward that gets lost.
_comment_portraits: W04-PORTRAITS, 2026-09-04 (owner directive 8b): every conversation now names its speaker's own plate, rendered from the installed rig the world stands that speaker in by tools/_capture_portraits.gd (Halda: villager_ranger with her iron-grey hair; Mira/Tam: the farmer and smith presets; Oskar and the male-rig villagers: villager_male; the South Bridge grunt: grunt_a, the base data/config/bands/band1_lower_meadows/trainers.json gives him). tests/test_dialogue_portraits.gd holds the line: no speaker other than the player may resolve to trainer.png.

tournament_halda.speaker: Halda
lines: Halda. I keep the board and I keep the draw honest — two jobs, this village.
Eight slots, four bouts, then two, then one.

tournament_halda_closed.speaker: Halda
lines: You'll want the tournament, then. Everyone does, first week.
Rule's the rule: no name on that board without a proper team behind it. One creature's a favourite, not a team.
Fill out all five places, then we'll talk.

tournament_halda_register.speaker: Halda
lines: You want your name on the board? Here's what I need to see first.
Five creatures. Your whole team, trained till they can stand in the ring.

lines.text: A real camp: tent, fire, bedroll. Build a Creature Bed, let one recover there, then come back rested, fed and happy.

lines: No walls or workshop required. I need proof you can keep a team, not a house.

tournament_halda_train.speaker: Halda
tournament_halda_train._comment_registration: TOURNAMENT-FLOW-0903. This can be a player's FIRST-EVER conversation with Halda -- one who built the whole roster before ever walking up to her skips `tournament_halda_register` entirely (village_npcs.json's own branch order), so this line also writes the opening handoff. Owner playtest 2026-09-03 item 2: 'even after I had everything, I had to talk to the starter several times' -- the fix is that a ready-enough team is never told the register speech at all, and every branch that could be the first meeting still marks it met.
lines: All five. Good. Now look at them.
Half that lot have never taken a real hit. I'd be signing them up for a hiding.

lines.text: Feed them. Rest them — a Creature Bed or your own bedroll, either does it. Get them to level five, then we'll talk.

tournament_halda_condition.speaker: Halda
tournament_halda_condition._comment: RG19-spec/D68. The entry gate the owner named in his own words: 'They have to be well rested, well fed, and happy.' Shown when the team is big enough and levelled enough but not in shape. Deliberately written as a reason and a to-do list, not a refusal -- she names the three things and where to go and do them, and the team screen's own condition line says WHICH creature is short of WHICH. The thresholds are in data/config/creature_condition.json and are not repeated here or anywhere else.
tournament_halda_condition._comment_registration: TOURNAMENT-FLOW-0903, same reasoning as tournament_halda_train's own comment: this can be a first meeting too, so it also writes the opening handoff.
lines: Levels aren't the whole of it. Look at the state of them.
That one's dead on its feet, and that one hasn't eaten since you found it. Tired creatures in front of a crowd doesn't go well for anyone.

lines.text: Beds at home, a proper feed, some time where nothing's trying to bite them. Then I'll put your name up.

tournament_halda_camp.speaker: Halda
tournament_halda_camp._comment_registration: TOURNAMENT-FLOW-0903, same reasoning as tournament_halda_train's own comment: this can be a first meeting too, so it also writes the opening handoff.
lines: They look strong enough. Now show me they have somewhere safe to come back to.

lines.text: A proper camp, a Creature Bed, one real night of recovery. A team that can fight isn't yet a team you can keep.

tournament_halda_signup.speaker: Halda
tournament_halda_signup._comment_registration: TOURNAMENT-FLOW-0903. A team that was already fully ready -- five trained creatures, rested, fed and camped -- before it ever met Halda gets sign-up as its ONE and only conversation with her, so this line also writes the opening handoff that `tournament_halda_register` used to own alone.
lines: Now that's a team. Look at them stood there like they've done this before.

lines.text: Right. Slot one — I've drawn you Mira first. She'll not go easy on you for selling you a potion. Board's up behind me.

tournament_halda_champion.speaker: Halda
lines: Champion of the Lower Meadows. That goes on the board properly now.
Here — the pattern for a riding saddle. Oskar's, by rights; he said give it to whoever took the Meadowhart off him.
A Meadowhart will carry you once you've built one. Rootstone for the frame, and the only rootstone left is past the south crossing.

tournament_quarter.speaker: Mira
lines: First bout, then. Don't look at me like that — the meadow doesn't care who's nice to it either.

lines.text: Get yourselves into the ring. Whole team out this time — nothing held back.

tournament_quarter_begin.speaker: Mira
tournament_quarter_begin._comment: TOURNAMENT-FLOW-0903 / owner playtest 2026-09-03 item 3: 'you enter then you choose to start the battle'. The ring-entrance banter above no longer starts the fight itself -- it only sets tournament_quarter_at_ring -- so a second, deliberate greeting is what actually opens it. Short on purpose: the owner wants ceremony, not delay.

lines.text: Ring's yours. Begin the round whenever you're ready.

tournament_quarter_beaten.speaker: Mira
lines: Out in the first. Well. Somebody's got to be, and I'd rather it was to you.

tournament_semi.speaker: Tam
lines: Semi-final. Fen put up more than the board says — I've a limp to prove it.

lines.text: Get into the ring. You know my lesson — let's see if you learned it or just heard it.
Ring's yours. Begin the round whenever you're ready.

tournament_semi_beaten.speaker: Tam
lines: Switched on me twice and I never saw the second one coming. That's the lesson, that is.

tournament_final.speaker: Oskar
lines: Final. Bryn took me to the last creature in the semi and I'm still short of breath.
You'll not have seen this one on the road. She's not a fighter by trade — she's a road, if you know how to sit on her.

lines.text: Beat her and the pattern's yours. Get into the ring.
Ring's yours. Begin the round whenever you're ready.

tournament_final_beaten.speaker: Oskar
tournament_final_beaten._comment_heal_party: G3-OPENING-FIX-0904 (2.10), the owner instruction 'give revives after the tournament' (2026-09-03). The tournament's three rounds reliably leave three of five creatures on 0 HP, and this is the one line every player who wins the final sees -- unlike tournament_halda_champion, which needs a separate walk back to Halda and, by its own _comment_saddle above, is optional (the saddle pattern itself is already granted by tournament_final_oskar's reward.flags whether or not that walk happens). Putting the heal here means it lands on the exact state the tournament produces, for every winner, not only the ones who go looking for Halda afterward.

lines.text: Took the Meadowhart off me fair. Go and see Halda — the pattern's hers to hand over, and I'll not go back on it.

south_bridge_grunt_challenge.speaker: Tether Grunt
lines: Far side's closed. Company business. Go back up the road.
Two of mine, nothing special. Shouldn't take long.

lines.text: You're not walking round me and you're not talking round me. Fine. Beat me and the key's yours — that's not policy, that's mine.

south_bridge_grunt_beaten.speaker: Tether Grunt
lines: Take it. I'll tell them you had one already.
Straight over, don't stop on the span. Nothing down there but the old road.

old_champion_challenge.speaker: Old Bram
old_champion_challenge._comment: Prompt 30's Old Champion: 'character/trainer history and a memorable battle or lesson using an existing NPC rig/team'. The history is Team Tether's arrival told from the losing side, which is the same story the site front door tells and the same one Grandpa is too old to finish -- so this is canon being said by somebody else, not a new thread. He never asks the player for anything and sets no flag until he is beaten: prompt 30 forbids the fetch-quest template and this is the opposite of one.
lines: Sit if you like. I've not got anywhere to be.
You'll be the one they're all talking about. Won the ribbon down in the square.

lines.text: I won it too, once. Held it eleven years.

lines: Then Tether came up the road with their pylons and paperwork, and I went to the bridge to tell them no. I was fifty-three with two creatures who'd never lost. Neither fact helped.

lines.text: You're going that way. I'd like to know if it's worth me hoping. Show me.

old_champion_beaten.speaker: Old Bram
old_champion_beaten._comment: The payoff line. The items and coins are granted by the trainer's own `reward` block the moment the fight is won (data/config/bands/band1_lower_meadows/trainers.json), so a player who walks off and never speaks to him again keeps them -- this is the acknowledgement, not the delivery. The last two lines are the ONLY place the elder mosshell (spawns.json order 1900) is named anywhere in the game. Prompt 30: some optional content should be found by curiosity, and secrets should not be pre-labelled on the map, so the elder has no marker -- but a player who did the harder optional thing gets told where the other one is, which makes the two a chain instead of two icons.
lines: Ha. Well.
First time in nine years I've enjoyed losing.
Take the orbs. You'll need them — the far side of that bridge doesn't hand anything over.

One more thing, since you've earned it. West of the pond, past where the path bends away, there's a hollow that stays green when everything round it burns off. A mosshell lives down there, older than I am.
I've never been able to take it. You might. Mind — it sees you coming a long way off.

meadowhart_herd_sighting.speaker: Rae
meadowhart_herd_sighting._comment: T3-ACTIVITIES, spec sec6's 'Meadowhart Herd: discovery activity that points toward the Riding Saddle progression'. Same OF30 one-time-gift shape Tam's tool handover uses: the discovery flag on the first line, the reward and the objective's own completion flag together on the last.

lines.text: Careful, don't come at them straight on -- they'll bolt. I've been sitting here the better part of an hour just watching them move.

lines: That's the same stock the tournament champion rides, near as I can tell. Once you've got rootstone worked out and a saddle frame built, one of these would carry you the same way.
For now, just look a while. It's worth the walk out here.

lines.text: Here -- I've got no use for these, but you might.

meadowhart_herd_greeting.speaker: Rae
lines: Still my favourite spot in the whole band. They come back most evenings.

broken_cart_broken.speaker: Coll
broken_cart_broken._comment: T3-ACTIVITIES, spec sec6's 'Broken Cart: gather materials to repair a bridgehand's cart'. No `battle:`/`give:` effect here -- `cart_repair.gd` owns the actual gather-and-hand-over check (item_gate.gd) and only opens the dialogue panel to report the result; this is what a player sees before they are carrying everything.
lines: Wheel's cracked, axle's split, and I've got nothing left in the box to fix either one.
Wood for the wheel, stone to true the axle bed, fiber for the lashings -- bring me those and I can still get this off the shoulder before dark.

broken_cart_repaired.speaker: Coll
lines: That's everything. Give me an hour and this'll be rolling again.
Not many stop to help a stranger's cart. I won't forget it.

shepherd_the_rise_challenge.speaker: Dara
shepherd_the_rise_challenge._comment: WORLD-CONTENT, docs/specs/BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md place 2: 'teaches nothing, is a fight you can see coming'. No lesson, no fetch, no flag until beaten -- a plain first fight on the open road, the shape prompt 30 asks optional field trainers to have.
lines: Gate's not far behind you. Long way to anywhere from here, if you're not ready for it.
I mind this stretch. Trailpups mostly -- yours look fresh off the practice field, same as mine were once.

lines.text: Two of mine against your two, then. See how fresh really holds up.

shepherd_the_rise_defeated.speaker: Dara
lines: Ha! Faster on their feet than I gave you credit for.
Keep to the road. Long field ahead, then the water. Mind the bridge before you get there -- Tether's got somebody posted on it now.

wanderer_trail_camp_challenge.speaker: Gil
wanderer_trail_camp_challenge._comment: WORLD-CONTENT, docs/specs/BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md place 4. The second and harder of the two new field trainers, deep enough into the Long Field that it reads as the road's own difficulty climbing toward the South Bridge checkpoint rather than a repeat of the Rise's gentler fight.
lines: Another one bound for the crossing. They're not letting much through without a fuss these days.
I've walked this road longer than most who try it. My team's earned its keep.

lines.text: Let's see what you've learned since the village, then.

wanderer_trail_camp_defeated.speaker: Gil
lines: Well fought. You've come a long way from whatever field you started in.
Camp's just up ahead if you need it. After that it's a straight run to the bridge -- and whoever's standing on it.

pond_fisher_greeting.speaker: Nan
pond_fisher_greeting._comment: WORLD-CONTENT, docs/specs/BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md place 3: 'a fisher NPC who mentions the South Bridge and the captured keeper (dialogue only, no fight)'. The captured keeper is the relay's own captive (data/dialogue/relay.json's Sela, freed via `captive_rescued`; MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md sec on the river crossing: 'the bridge keeper / ranger / researcher who knows the mechanism has been captured'), named here only as rumour a Band 1 fisher would plausibly have heard -- the player has no way to know who she is yet, which is the point of a rumour this early.
lines: Quiet out here since the company came through. Even the fish keep low these days.
Word's gone round they've got someone locked up past that bridge. One of the border scouts, so they say. Nobody's seen her since.
You crossing? Mind the one standing watch. He won't just wave you through.
